title: Hotset Trimmer: per-layer KV residency heuristics + streaming-batch rampdown for long-context variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a model-aware 'hotset trimmer' that reduces GPU KV residency by probabilistically evicting low-value entries using per-layer residency heuristics and a sliding TTL curve. Target long-context model variants (Llama-3-70B-64k, Mistral-7B-65k, Qwen-14-128k) where KV working sets grow nonlinearly. Combine this with a streaming-batch rampdown policy that reduces batch packing aggressiveness as memory pressure rises to keep tail latency within SLOs. The goal is to lower peak memory by 10-25% on common long-dialogue workloads while preserving generation quality and p50/p95 latency bounds.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented per-layer residency scoring that computes an eviction priority for KV shards and tokens
Hotset trimmer toggles per-model and per-variant via model profile config
Streaming-batch rampdown reduces batch size adaptively under defined watermarks and preserves p50 latency within 10% of baseline
Benchmarks show >=10% reduction in peak GPU memory for at least two target model variants on synthetic long-dialogue trace
End-to-end integration tests pass in dedicated staging, and a canary rollout plan validated on 5% traffic without dropped requests
updates: 2026-01-20: Ticket created after spike analysis showed long-tail memory growth on Mistral/LLama traces.
2026-01-28: Architecture proposal reviewed — agreed to combine probabilistic eviction with per-layer TTLs rather than pure LRU to avoid pathological eviction during repetitive prompts.

2026-02-05: Prototype implemented: per-layer counters + exponential decay TTL. Initial microbench shows 12% reduction in resident KV entries for a 64k Llama trace but small increase in rerolls for repeated context tokens.

2026-02-18: Bench harness extended to include Qwen-14-128k traces and real customer anonymized logs (consent verified). Observed model-specific differences: Qwen benefits more from coarser-grained shard eviction; Llama needs finer per-layer granularity.

2026-02-25: Introduced streaming-batch rampdown: when memory watermark > 0.75, reduce max continuous batch window from 32->8 and prioritize single-request latency. Microbench p95 improved by 8% versus naive eviction-only approach.

2026-03-03: Design review with runtime and infra — decision to surface three knobs in model profiles: hotset_threshold, per_layer_decay_ms, rampdown_watermarks. Runtime team will expose metrics for investigation (hotset_size, eviction_rate).
2026-03-09: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289) with hotset trimmer core. Initial CI failures fixed; integration tests now passing on x86-GPU staging fleet.
2026-03-10: Canary gating: ready for 5% canary in dedicated pool; monitoring dashboards prepared. Awaiting approvals for canary start from SRE and Product.
2026-03-11: Added regression alert rule for generation perplexity drift tied to prompt sets (eval-suite-3) to detect quality regressions post-rollout.
comments: Zoe Chen (runtime): We should ensure eviction metadata is compact — added suggestion to pack per-layer counters into 16-bit rolls to avoid extra allocation pressure.
Liam O'Connor (infra): Can we expose a fallback to persistent cold-cache on disk for very large contexts? Not for this sprint but added to backlog.
Priya Sharma (PM): Prioritize preserving customer-facing latencies; if memory tradeoff causes >15% p95 regression revert to conservative profile.
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction priority computation and per-layer TTL decay
Microbench: run synthetic long-dialogue traces for Llama-3-70B-64k, Mistral-7B-65k, Qwen-14-128k comparing baseline vs trimmer
Integration test: end-to-end generation on staging with streaming enabled and batch rampdown active
Canary: 5% traffic in dedicated pool for 72 hours with strict SLO monitoring
Quality checks: run eval-suite-3 prompt sets and compare token-level distributions and perplexity thresholds
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge feature flag behind model-profile rollout and start internal canary on staging fleet
Stage 2: 5% canary on dedicated runtime for 72 hours (monitor memory, p50/p95 latency, perplexity)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% if no regressions, then full enablement for selected models
Rollback: Toggle model_profile to off if regression alert fires or SRE requests revert
risks: Evicting tokens that are reused later in the same conversation could increase recompute and token costs
Complex per-layer heuristics may add CPU overhead — need to minimize per-token work in hot path
Quality regressions undetected by coarse eval sets — mitigated by targeted prompt suites and regression alerts
benchmarks: Baseline (Llama-3-70B-64k): peak resident KV 24.3 GB, p95 latency 512 ms
Prototype (hotset trimmer): peak resident KV 20.9 GB (-14%), p95 latency 540 ms (+5.5%)
With streaming-batch rampdown: peak resident KV 19.8 GB (-18.5%), p95 latency 498 ms (-2.7% vs baseline)
